## Appearance

In his youth, he was characterized by delicate, refined features and a halo of natural chestnut or brown curls, accompanied by very dark blue eyes. By the age of sixteen, his curls had been replaced by close-cropped brown locks. He eventually grew into a splendid six-foot tall man.

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P7](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0007), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v3 ch.People P13](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0013), [v3 ch.Revelation P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), +1 more_

## Personality

Paul Irving is an exceptionally imaginative child and a recognized genius who also possesses a remarkably gentlemanly and cleanly demeanor. Known for his capability and manliness in schoolyard games, he is exceptionally well-liked. Furthermore, he uses his standing among the older students to actively protect and assist the younger boys.

_Sources: [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road P3](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0003), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P5](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0005), +1 more_

## History

Paul Irving was born in the United [States](../codex/places.md#states), but three years after his mother passed away, he moved to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) to live with his grandmother. He became a pupil of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and quickly stood out as her favorite student due to his bright, imaginative nature and his fondness for poetic stories. Outside of school, Paul shared his creative ideas through letters and verse, including written descriptions of imaginary friends who lived along the shore. His rich inner life made him a natural companion for [Anne](../character/anne.md), who visited him at his home and accompanied him on walks to the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) cemetery and [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge) to visit Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md). During these visits, Paul bonded deeply with Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) over their shared imaginative spirit, unaware at first of her history with his father, [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md). When [Stephen](../character/stephen-irving.md) returned to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) and reconciled with Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md), Paul shared in the family's joy surrounding their eventual wedding. Over time, his own poetry gained public recognition and was published in magazines. As he grew older, he maintained his affection for his former teacher, attending Anne's wedding at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) prior to her departure for [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary.

_Sources: [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P2](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0002), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P14](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0014), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P15](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0015), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P16](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0016), +494 more_

## Quotes

> "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)

> "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058)

> "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021)

> "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)

> “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--paul-irving.md)

Paul Irving is [Anne](../character/anne.md) Shirley's student at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school and quickly becomes her favorite pupil. The two share a bright, imaginative nature and form a close bond, frequently talking after school and sharing personal letters about their creative ideas. Paul often gifts [Anne](../character/anne.md) wild orchids, and she takes a warm interest in his upbringing and personal life.

- Friend of — teacher and student friendship  <sub>[v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021), [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), +4 more</sub>
- Student of — schoolteacher  <sub>[v2 I An Irate Neighbor P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 XXVI Around the Bend P24](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0024), +3 more</sub>

### [Grandma Irving](../character/grandma-irving.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/grandma-irving--paul-irving.md)

[Grandma Irving](../character/grandma-irving.md) is Paul's grandmother who raises him and enforces strict domestic rules, which Paul occasionally contrasts with his imaginative world. Despite her strictness, she cares for Paul, and town residents regularly discuss both her and Paul's unique personality. Paul respects her, though he finds solace in discussing his feelings and thoughts about his deceased mother and family history with others.

- Relative of — grandmother  <sub>[v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P12](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0012), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P3](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0003), [v2 XXIII Miss Lavendar’s Romance P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), +4 more</sub>

### [Irving](../character/irving.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/irving--paul-irving.md)

[Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md) is Paul's father. Paul lives apart from him for a time, but their lives intersect closely when [Stephen](../character/stephen-irving.md) returns to reconnect with his old love, Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md). Paul candidly discusses the romantic turn of events surrounding his father's reunion and impending wedding with [Anne](../character/anne.md).

- Child of — father  <sub>[v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022), [v2 XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace P45](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0045), [v2 XXIX Poetry and Prose P1](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0001)</sub>

### [Lavendar Lewis](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/lavendar-lewis--paul-irving.md)

Miss [Lavendar Lewis](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and Paul are kindred spirits who share a deep imaginative connection. During visits to [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge), Paul plays in her garden and listens to her stories about an imaginary dream-boy, a romantic concept that resonates strongly with Paul's own inner world. They form a loving bond that culminates in Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) marrying Paul's father.

- Friend of — kindred spirits sharing stories and imagination in the garden  <sub>[v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051)</sub>

### [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/lynde--paul-irving.md)

[Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) is an [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) neighbor who takes a fond interest in Paul. She often discusses his unique imagination with other town mothers and monitors his progress in school.

- Friend of — fond of the young boy  <sub>[v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>

### [Twin Sailors](../character/twin-sailors.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/paul-irving--twin-sailors.md)

The [Twin Sailors](../character/twin-sailors.md) are imaginary characters invented by Paul, whom he conceives as rock people that come ashore to speak with him. Paul incorporates them into whimsical tales of sailing into moonglades, though he explicitly clarifies in his writing that they are only imaginative stories rather than real people.

- presumed Friend of — imaginary rock people who come ashore to talk with him  <sub>[v2 XI Facts and Fancies P42](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0042)</sub>
